feed.title: Vidhana — Sri Lankan IRD tax and VAT gazettes — income-tax
feed.subtitle: What changed in the Sri Lankan Inland Revenue gazettes, and what the rule is now. Derived from https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/sitepages/gazette.aspx?menuid=1602

entry.title: 2414/14 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017, Regulations under Section 86 (7)
entry.content:
From 1 January 2025, withholding agents making payments outside Sri Lanka must withhold the applicable tax on payments to non-residents and obtain a Tax Clearance Certificate before remitting the money, unless the payment falls within the listed exemptions. The rules also require relevant payment details to be reported in withholding tax statements; banks and authorised dealers must collect remittance information and submit monthly schedules to Inland Revenue.
Effective from 2025-01-01.
Affects: income taxpayers; withholding agents.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2024_2414-14_E.pdf

entry.title: 2378/33 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017, Notice under Subsection (3) of Section 145
entry.content:
The Commissioner General has specified that tax payments under the Inland Revenue Act must be made only by cash deposit, pay order or bank draft, or through the Online Tax Payments Platform (OTPP). This sets the permitted payment methods for affected tax payments.
Effective from 2024-04-04.
Affects: employers; income taxpayers; withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2024_2378-33_E.pdf

entry.title: 2376/25 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act, no. 24 of 2017, Regulation under Section 123 (8)
entry.content:
From 1 April 2024, the regulation requires specified government registries, government contracting officers, financial institutions and the Colombo Stock Exchange to regularly provide detailed information to the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue. The information covers property and lease transactions, companies and shareholders, vehicles, government contracts, bank accounts and loans, and investments and securities transactions. The Commissioner General will separately notify each person or institution when its reporting must begin; information not previously maintained must be started from 1 July 2024.
Effective from 2024-04-01.
Affects: employers; income taxpayers; withholding agents.
(Summary confidence: low. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2024_2376-25_E.pdf

entry.title: 2334/21 [income-tax] new: Notice made Under Section 102 of Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017
entry.content:
Additional classes of resident individuals must register under Section 102 of the Inland Revenue Act, unless they were already registered when this notice was issued. From 1 June 2023, this includes specified professionals, business registrants, certain vehicle and property owners, some employees, building-plan applicants, and individuals earning specified amounts from services in Sri Lanka; from 1 January 2024, it also covers individuals aged 18 or over who are not in Part A.
Effective from 2023-06-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2023_2334-21_E.pdf

entry.title: 2312/16 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act, no. 24 of 2017, Notice under Section 83A
entry.content:
From 1 January 2023, employers must withhold employment-income tax using different tax tables for regular pay, lump sums, terminal benefits, multiple or secondary employments, and other specified payments. Employees with more than one employment must nominate a Primary Employment and provide declarations and, when changing jobs, previous withholding certificates. Employers must file annual employee payment and tax details, issue withholding certificates, and keep payroll and tax records for at least five years.
Effective from 2023-01-01.
Affects: employers; income taxpayers; withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2312-16_E.pdf

entry.title: 2303/05 [income-tax] rescinds 2064/57
entry.content:
From 1 April 2022, financial institutions calculating banking-business profits may not deduct specific debt-claim provisions for the listed categories, including loans to associates, persons outside Sri Lanka and employees, or Stage 1 and Stage 2 credit facilities. They must maintain records of specific debt-claim provisions separately for Stage 1, 2 and 3 facilities using the prescribed format. This notice rescinds Gazette Extraordinary No. 2064/57 from the same date.
Rescinds 2064/57 — Notice in relation to specific provision for a debt claim made by a person conducting a banking business.
Effective from 2022-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2303-05_E.pdf

entry.title: 2258/18 [income-tax] new: Notice under Paragraph 10 of Sixth Schedule
entry.content:
This notice sets the method for calculating the local value added in goods and services for the additional deduction available for qualifying marketing and communication expenses. Businesses claiming that deduction must keep calculation worksheets, expense lists, supplier and associated-person details, contracts, and supporting invoices or tax invoices. It covers sellers of goods, manufacturers’ distributors undertaking marketing and communication, and service suppliers, including mixed or composite services.
Effective from 2021-12-14.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2021_2258-18_E.pdf

entry.title: 2234/06 [income-tax] new: Information technology and enabled services prescribe for the purpose of Subparagraph (ii) of Paragraph (u) of Third Schedule of the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 as amended by the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 10 of 2021,
entry.content:
This Order prescribes information technology and enabled services for the tax treatment referred to in the Third Schedule of the Inland Revenue Act, effective from 1 January 2020. Businesses providing the listed services must meet conditions including, from 1 April 2020, a minimum 70% share of local technical employees for specified software services, or at least 50% local value addition for other listed services; businesses formed by splitting an existing business do not qualify.
Effective from 2020-01-01.
Affects: employers; income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2021_2234-06_E.pdf

entry.title: 2232/06 [income-tax] new: Notice under Section 5,10, First Schedule and Third Schedule
entry.content:
This notice sets conditions for pension, provident, gratuity and savings funds approved by the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue. An employer’s total contributions to terminal-benefit funds, including EPF and ETF, must not exceed 25% of its total salary bill for the accounting year; approved funds must also meet specified investment limits. EPF and ETF are treated as approved funds regardless of these conditions.
Effective from 2021-06-14.
Affects: employers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/IR_2021_2232-06_E.pdf

entry.title: 2232/05 [income-tax] new: Guidelines under Section 57 of the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 10 of 2021
entry.content:
These guidelines explain how to calculate income tax for the 2019/2020 year of assessment after the 2021 amendments. Individuals must divide income and reliefs between the periods before and after 1 January 2020, while partnerships and other entities must apply the specified apportionment, tax rates, withholding-tax and tax-credit rules. Partnerships became liable for income tax on taxable income from 1 January 2020.
Effective from 2020-01-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2232-05_E.pdf

entry.title: 2217/07 [income-tax] rescinds 2104/04
entry.content:
These regulations replace Gazette Extraordinary No. 2104/4 and apply from 1 April 2020. They require income taxpayers carrying out controlled transactions with associated enterprises to apply arm’s-length pricing and, where the stated thresholds apply, maintain transfer-pricing files, submit an annual disclosure form, and meet country-by-country reporting or notification requirements. They also set the recognised pricing methods, penalties for non-compliance, and rules for advance pricing agreements.
Rescinds 2104/04 — Regulations on Transfer Pricing.
Effective from 2020-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/TP_2021_ 2217-07_E.pdf

entry.title: 2194/50 [income-tax] rescinds 2064/63
entry.content:
This notice replaces Schedule 01 in Gazette 2064/63 and sets the requirements for registering an individual as an authorized representative under the Inland Revenue Act. Applicants must generally be Sri Lankan citizens and residents aged at least 21, meet one of the listed professional or experience-based qualifications, and have none of the stated disqualifications. The Commissioner General may register or remove representatives and must publish the register at least once a year.
Rescinds 2064/63 — Notify the requirements to registered as Authorized Representative.
Effective from 2020-09-23.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2020_2194-50_E.pdf

entry.title: 2130/02 [income-tax] rescinds 2064/54
entry.content:
This regulation replaces item (i) of the Schedule issued in Gazette 2064/54. The replacement covers income tax, super tax, surtax, or similar taxes paid in another country, while excluding any amount above the foreign tax credit allowed under sections 80 and 81 of the Inland Revenue Act. It applies from 1 April 2018.
Rescinds 2064/54 — Notification specify the taxes or other levies which the deductions shall not be made in calculating a person's income.
Effective from 2019-07-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2130-02_E.pdf

entry.title: 2104/04 [income-tax] rescinds 1823/05
entry.content:
These regulations introduced transfer pricing rules for transactions between associated enterprises, requiring them to use arm’s-length pricing and keep supporting records. Affected taxpayers also had to submit transfer pricing information with their income tax return, with additional documentation requirements for larger transactions and multinational groups. The rules in this gazette were later rescinded and replaced by Gazette 2217/07, effective from 1 April 2020; the replacement applies for periods from that date.
Rescinds 1823/05 — Inland Revenue Act, No. 10 of 2006 - Transfer Pricing Regulations on International Transactions.
The current document in this rule is now 2217/07 (2021-03-02).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2104-04_E.pdf

entry.title: 2089/01 [income-tax] amends 2064/53
entry.content:
This Order amends Gazette Extraordinary No. 2064/53. It preserves the tax treatment promised in qualifying agreements entered into with the Board of Investment before April 2018: the enterprise’s profits and income, and dividends it pays, remain exempt or continue to be taxed using the agreed basis or rate under the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017.
Amends 2064/53 — Order under Sec. 194 of Inland Revenue Act, no 24 of 2017, that the Regulations of Transitional Provisions.
Effective from 2018-09-17.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2089-01_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/64 [income-tax] new: Notify the fee to be charged in relation to an application for a private ruling requested by a tax payer.
entry.content:
A taxpayer requesting a private ruling from the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue must pay a fee of Rs. 25,000.00 for the application. The notice does not state a separate commencement date, so the fee applies as specified in this notice from its publication date context.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-64_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/63 [income-tax] new: Notify the requirements to registered as Authorized Representative
entry.content:
This notice sets the eligibility requirements for an individual to register as an authorized representative under the Inland Revenue Act, including age, Sri Lankan residency and citizenship, specified tax or accounting qualifications, experience and fitness requirements. It also provides for registration, removal from the register and annual publication of registered representatives. The requirements in this notice were replaced by Gazette 2194/50 on 23 September 2020; as amended, the replacement schedule also recognises Chartered Tax Advisors and changes some qualification wording.
The current document in this rule is now 2194/50 (2020-09-23).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-63_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/60 [income-tax] new: Notice specify the withhold tax from payments where the payments made to any employee and rates of tax to be withheld from such payments.
entry.content:
From 1 April 2018, employers must withhold income tax from employee payments using the applicable tax table for regular pay, lump sums, terminal benefits, non-citizen employees, multiple or secondary employments, and tax paid by the employer on an employee’s behalf. Employers must also manage primary-employment declarations, issue withholding certificates, file annual employee and tax details, and keep relevant records for at least five years.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: employers; withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-60_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/59 [income-tax] new: Notice specify the Capital gain tax return and schedules to be furnished
entry.content:
People liable for Capital Gains Tax on investment assets realised on or after 1 April 2018 must submit the specified Capital Gain Tax return and schedules. The filing deadline is generally one month after the realisation; a separate rule applies when a resident individual’s total gains exceed Rs. 600,000, and joint ownership can require each resident individual to file. The prescribed forms are Annex I (Asmt_CGT_001_E) and Annex II (Asmt_CGT_002_E).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: low. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-59_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/58 [income-tax] new: Notice specify the circumstances under which a tax payer may designate an authorized representative
entry.content:
From 1 April 2018, an income taxpayer may designate an authorized representative to communicate with the Inland Revenue Department in specified matters. These include registration and profile changes, tax returns, private rulings, reviews, refunds, extensions of time, investigations, capital gains tax returns, and any other matter specifically authorized in writing.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-58_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/57 [income-tax] new: Notice in relation to specific provision for a debt claim made by a person conducting a banking business
entry.content:
The 2018 notice set limits on which provisions for debt claims a banking business could deduct when calculating taxable banking profits, including provisions for loans to associated persons or persons outside Sri Lanka. It was rescinded by Gazette 2303/05 with effect from 1 April 2022 and replaced by new specifications, which also exclude certain pawning, employee and multiple-facility claims and Stage 1 and Stage 2 impairment charges. The 2018 rule therefore no longer applies.
The current document in this rule is now 2303/05 (2022-10-25).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-57_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/56 [income-tax] new: Notice in relation to the any period for which interest on a blended loan
entry.content:
This notice addresses the period used when interest on a blended loan is compounded. It says that another period recognised under generally accepted accounting principles is specified, but it does not identify that period in the document, so the practical calculation rule cannot be determined from this notice alone.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: low. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-56_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/55 [income-tax] new: Notice in relation to the circumstances in which losses on financial instruments
entry.content:
Losses on a financial instrument may be offset only against gains from the same type of financial instrument. This sets the required tax treatment for taxpayers reporting such financial instrument losses and gains.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-55_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/54 [income-tax] new: Notification specify the taxes or other levies which the deductions shall not be made in calculating a person's income
entry.content:
When calculating a person’s income, income taxpayers must not deduct the listed taxes and levies, including Economic Service Charge, certain taxes on financial services, Crop Insurance Levy, and specified levies under the Finance Act. Item (i) was later amended by Gazette 2130/02 to cover comparable income taxes paid in any country, subject to the foreign tax credit limitation, and applies from 1 April 2018.
The current document in this rule is now 2130/02 (2019-07-01).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-54_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/53 [income-tax] new: Order under Sec. 194 of Inland Revenue Act, no 24 of 2017, that the Regulations of Transitional Provisions
entry.content:
These transitional rules preserve certain tax exemptions, concessionary rates, losses, allowances, depreciation treatment, finance-lease calculations, approvals and notional tax credits when the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 replaced the earlier tax law from 1 April 2018. As amended by Gazette 2089/01 from 17 September 2018, qualifying enterprises with pre-April 2018 Board of Investment agreements may also continue their agreed exemptions or reduced rates for dividends paid by those enterprises.
The current document in this rule is now 2089/01 (2018-09-17).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-53_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/52 [income-tax] new: Order under Inland Revenue Act, No 24 of 2017, (e) III of 3rd Schedule that the official emoluments of any individual who is employed by the Asian Development Bank.
entry.content:
From 1 April 2018, official emoluments paid to an individual employed by the Asian Development Bank are treated as exempt amounts for the purposes of the Third Schedule of the Inland Revenue Act. This means those emoluments are excluded from the relevant income-tax calculation.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-52_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/51 [income-tax] new: Order under Sec. 85 of Inland Revenue Act, No 24 of 2017, as being the Service's rendered with a Source in Sri Lanka and Pays to a resident Individual being
entry.content:
For section 85 of the Inland Revenue Act, these regulations prescribe categories of services treated as having a source in Sri Lanka when paid to a resident individual, including professional, construction, security, management, vocational and similar services. They also prescribe a 2% rate when a resident person makes a payment to a non-resident person. The regulations apply from 1 April 2018.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-51_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/50 [income-tax] new: Deduction of Income Tax from Interest Payment to a Senior citizen on money deposite in Banks or Financial Institutions, From 01.04.2018
entry.content:
From 1 April 2018, banks and financial institutions must withhold income tax at 5% on a senior citizen’s interest income above Rs. 1,500,000 for the year of assessment. Senior citizens must submit a declaration each year for each account, stating whether the threshold is exceeded or the relief has already been used elsewhere; false or misleading declarations are treated as statements made to a tax official.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers; withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-50_E.pdf

entry.title: 2006/37 [income-tax] rescinds 1487/03, 1712/18
entry.content:
From 9 February 2017, new rules govern approval and registration of authorized representatives under the Inland Revenue Act. They set eligibility and disqualification requirements, require applicants to apply to the Commissioner General, and require an annual Gazette list of approved representatives. The rules replace the 2007 regulations and their 2011 amendment.
Rescinds 1487/03 — The Inland Revenue Act - The Approval of Authorized Representatives Regulations No.1 of 2006.
Rescinds 1712/18 — Amendment to the Authorized Representative Regulations No. 1 of 2006 published in Gaz. Ex. No. 1487/3 of 05.03.2007.
Effective from 2017-02-09.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2017_2006_37_E.pdf

entry.title: 1991/35 [income-tax] new: The Facilitation of the Implementation of Revenue Administration Management Information System (RAMIS)
entry.content:
These regulations introduce electronic submission of tax returns, supporting documents and schedules through the Inland Revenue Department’s RAMIS web portal, in the format and manner specified by the Commissioner General. They also set rules for authorised staff and tax agents, system-generated notices and assessments, temporary acknowledgements, and electronic record storage. No commencement or effective date is stated in the document.
Effective from 2016-11-02.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2016_1991_35_E.pdf

entry.title: 1960/42 [income-tax] amends 1907/26
entry.content:
This notice replaces Part IA of Gazette Extraordinary No. 1907/26 with a revised transfer pricing disclosure form. Income taxpayers must use the form to report transactions with associated undertakings, including receipts, payments, loans, pricing methods, documentation, financial information and certification, for years of assessment beginning on or after 1 April 2015.
Amends 1907/26 — Amending the Gaz. Ex. Ord. No. 1479/6 of 09.01.2017 under Section 213 of Inland Revenue Act, No. 10 of 2006.
Effective from 2016-03-31.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2016_1960_42_E.pdf

entry.title: 1960/39 [income-tax] amends 1823/05
entry.content:
As amended, associated undertakings with transactions with other associated undertakings totalling at least Rs. 100 million in a year of assessment must submit transfer-pricing disclosures with their income tax return. Their director, principal officer or precedent partner must also submit a transfer-pricing certificate to the Commissioner General, with copies or inclusion in the company’s annual report as specified. The changes apply from 1 April 2015; where the relevant transactions are Rs. 10 million or less, the disclosure may generally be limited to the transaction records and related information.
Amends 1823/05 — Inland Revenue Act, No. 10 of 2006 - Transfer Pricing Regulations on International Transactions.
The current document in this rule is now 2217/07 (2021-03-02).
Effective from 2015-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2016_1960_39_E.pdf

entry.title: 1907/26 [income-tax] amends 1479/06
entry.content:
As amended by Gazette 1960/42, this notice requires the prescribed Part IA transfer-pricing disclosure form for income taxpayers’ transactions with associated undertakings. It covers disclosures by the taxpayer and certification by an approved accountant, including transaction details and the arm’s-length pricing methods used, for years of assessment beginning on or after 1 April 2015. The Part IA certificate originally inserted by this Gazette was replaced by the later notice.
Amends 1479/06 — The Inland Revenue Act No. 10 of 2006 - Notices under Section 107(2)(a) & Sec. 4(3).
The current document in this rule is now 1960/42 (2016-03-31).
Effective from 2015-03-25.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2015_1907_26_E.pdf

entry.title: 1857/08 [income-tax] new: Regulation made for adjustments made in the ascertainment of Profits or Income for Tax purposes in the preparation of Financial Statements in relation to any Year of Assessment commencing on or after 01.04.2012(SLRFS)
entry.content:
This regulation sets the tax treatment and required supporting information when income taxpayers prepare financial statements under Sri Lanka Financial Reporting Standards or Lanka Accounting Standards. It covers items such as depreciation, leases, revenue, financial instruments, impairment and foreign exchange, and requires specified schedules or reconciliations to be submitted with tax computations. It applies to years of assessment beginning on or after 1 April 2012, including adjustments to accounting figures when calculating taxable income.
Effective from 2014-04-09.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2014_1857_08_(E).pdf

entry.title: 1823/05 [income-tax] rescinds 1546/10
entry.content:
These regulations set the transfer-pricing rules for associated undertakings, including arm’s-length pricing methods and records that must be kept for international and certain other transactions. As amended by Gazette 1960/39, from 1 April 2015, associated undertakings with transactions of at least LKR 100 million had to submit transfer-pricing reports and a director, principal officer or precedent partner certificate with the income tax return. The regulations were later rescinded by Gazette 2104/04, effective 1 April 2018, and are no longer operative.
Rescinds 1546/10 — Inland Revenue Act No. 10 of 2006 Transfer Pricing Regulations.
The current document in this rule is now 2217/07 (2021-03-02).
Effective from 2013-08-12.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2013_1823_05 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1813/17 [income-tax] new: Amendment to Inland Revenue Act No. 10 of 2006 - Notice under Sec. 34 (2) (r)
entry.content:
This notice identifies named villages in nine districts for the purpose of Section 34(2)(r) of the Inland Revenue Act. It does not state a new filing, payment or other compliance deadline; its practical tax effect depends on the relief or rule provided by Section 34(2)(r).
Effective from 2013-06-06.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2013_1813_17 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1782/20 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act No. 10 of 2006 Notice under Sec. 34(2)(r) (Names of Villages)
entry.content:
This notice identifies four villages in the District of Kandy for the purpose of paragraph (r) of section 34(2) of the Inland Revenue Act. It does not state a new filing or payment deadline; it records the villages covered by that provision.
Effective from 2012-10-30.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2012_1782_20 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1728/13 [income-tax] amends 1704/18
entry.content:
This gazette changes the investment condition for pension, provident, gratuity and savings funds to be approved by the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue. Under the revised condition, at least 40% of fund money may be invested through deposits with the listed banks or in Government Securities, replacing the corresponding paragraph in Gazette Extraordinary No. 1704/18.
Amends 1704/18 — Inland Revenue Act, No. 10 of 2006 Notice under Sec 217.
Effective from 2011-10-19.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2011_1728_13 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1712/18 [income-tax] amends 1487/03
entry.content:
The 2011 amendment changed the qualifications and experience requirements for people seeking approval as authorized representatives under the Inland Revenue Act. As amended by Gazette 2006/37, effective 9 February 2017, the 2007 regulations and this amendment were rescinded and replaced by new Approval of Authorized Representative Regulations.
Amends 1487/03 — The Inland Revenue Act - The Approval of Authorized Representatives Regulations No.1 of 2006.
The current document in this rule is now 2006/37 (2017-02-15).
Effective from 2011-06-30.
Affects: employers; income taxpayers; withholding agents.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2011_1712_18 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1708/34 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act No. 10 of 2006. Order under Sec. 17A
entry.content:
This Order lists qualifying activities for new undertakings, including agriculture, manufacturing, tourism, infrastructure, renewable power, healthcare and software development. It provides income-tax exemption periods of 5, 6 or 7 years for qualifying investments of at least US$3 million, US$5 million or US$7 million respectively, provided the investment is completed within one year after the relevant exemption period begins. Additional conditions apply to export-oriented manufacturing and services provided outside Sri Lanka.
Effective from 2011-06-03.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2011_1708_34 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1706/18 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act No. 10 of 2006 Order under Sec. 4(2)
entry.content:
This order sets the taxable values for employee benefits provided by employers, effective from 1 April 2011. It covers shares and share options, employer-provided housing, private use of vehicles and motorcycles, and benefits such as insurance, meals, utilities, telephone costs and air tickets. Employers must use these prescribed values when calculating employment benefits, subject to exemptions under the Inland Revenue Act.

entry.title: 1704/18 [income-tax] rescinds 1599/13
entry.content:
This notice sets the conditions for pension, provident, gratuity and savings funds to be approved for Inland Revenue Act purposes. Employers’ total contributions to all such funds must not exceed 25% of their annual salary bill; the funds must also follow limits on investments, including at least 40% in deposits with specified banks or Government Securities, no more than 20% in listed debentures or other stocks, and the balance in other commercial-bank deposits. The position is as amended by Gazette 1728/13 (19 October 2011), which added the Regional Development Bank to the institutions eligible for the 40% investment requirement.
Rescinds 1599/13 — General Conditions for Provident, Gratuity, Pension or Saving Fund..

entry.content:

entry.title: 1487/08 [income-tax] new: The Inland Revenue Act - Re. Activities relating to infrastructure development
entry.content:
Companies engaged in specified infrastructure activities may qualify for an income tax exemption on their profits and income. The activities include airports, seaports, highways, railways, industrial parks, warehouses, sanitation and waste management, power, water services, urban housing or own center development, and hospitals; the exemption lasts 6 to 12 years depending on investment of Rs. 1,000 million or more, provided the investment is fully made within one year after commercial operations begin.
Effective from 2007-03-05.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/20071487_8(E).pdf

entry.title: 1487/07 [income-tax] new: The Inland Revenue Act - Re. Specified Undertaking in relation to a company
entry.content:
These regulations define which company projects qualify as a “specified undertaking” for the Section 17 income-tax exemption. Eligible projects include listed manufacturing, engineering, cold-storage or refrigerated transport, export production villages, offshore-company management or back-office operations, and projects with investment above Rs. 250 million. The company must provide evidence of its investment and must not reduce or withdraw that investment during the exemption period; otherwise, its profits and income become liable to income tax from the relevant year of assessment in which operations began.
Effective from 2007-03-05.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/20071487_7(E).pdf
